ENVE 200.title: Environmental Engineering Design and Decision Making
ENVE 200.description: Environmental Engineering design and decision-making, analysis tools and techniques, data illustration and other communication techniques, professional development including ethics and equity. Subject themes include water, air and soil. .

ENVE 201.title: Technical Communications for Environmental Engineering
ENVE 201.description: All aspects of technical communication, including report preparation, business correspondence, and oral presentation, applied to environmental engineering specific cases and projects.
ENVE 201.prerequisiteText: One of APSC_V 176, ENGL_V 110, ENGL_V 111, ENGL_V 112, ENGL_V 120, ENGL_V 121, WRDS_V 150

ENVE 202.title: Environmental Engineering Science
ENVE 202.description: Analysis of integrated environmental systems, quantification of fundamental chemical and biological processes, systems design, evaluation of environmental impact, future trends. .
ENVE 202.prerequisiteText: All of CIVL_V 204 and CHBE_V 241, and either CHEM_V 154 or all of CHEM_V 121, CHEM_V 123

ENVE 203.title: Environmental Engineering and Sustainability
ENVE 203.description: Sustainability vocabulary and systems theory relevant to environmental engineering practice, foundational sustainability topics including those relating to urban ecology, industrial ecology/circular economy, and humanitarian engineering, stakeholder analysis, communication, and adaptive change leadership skills

ENVE 301.title: Environmental Engineering Intermediate Design Project
ENVE 301.description: Real-time, fully-integrated, conceptual and detailed design experiences that address an ill-structured, socially and technically complex environmental engineering problem for communities with consideration to the cultural history and needs of the communities. Restricted to students in ENVE or ENVL with third-year or higher standing.

ENVE 401.title: Environmental Engineering Capstone Project
ENVE 401.description: Application of chemical, biological, and environmental science; engineering concepts; sustainable development and health and safety considerations; engineering economics; and life cycle analysis. Conceptual and detailed design for a multi-scale and complex environment health and protection problem. .
ENVE 401.prerequisiteText: All of CHBE_V 244, CHBE_V 373, ENVE_V 301 and fourth-year standing in ENVL
